articles.title: UN: Israeli forces made 280 incursions into Syria, detain 49 Syrians
articles.summary:
UN: Israeli forces made 280 incursions into Syria, detain 49 Syrians

Israel has carried out 280 armed incursions into Syria in September and currently detains 49 Syrians, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk has said.

Several released Syrian detainees have reported “allegations of torture and ill-treatment”, among other violations against them, according to a statement issued by Turk’s office on Friday. 

Israeli incursions into Syria in September -- marked by raids on homes, restrictions on movement, harassment and intimidation of civilians, arbitrary detention and destruction of livelihoods -- were the highest monthly number of incursions since the start of the year, the statement said.

articles.title: Trump says ICC sanctions aimed at defending Netanyahu and others
articles.summary:
Trump says ICC sanctions aimed at defending Netanyahu and others

US President Donald Trump has said Washington’s sanctions on the International Criminal Court were intended to defend Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and others from prosecution, not himself.

As Secretary of State Marco Rubio was explaining the rationale behind the sanctions, saying they were aimed at “bringing that court to heel”, Trump interrupted him and said: “Well, there is no information that they were after me. It could happen. But just so you know, but if he’s talking about it, that means that maybe ... he is not trying to defend me, he is trying to defend Bibi (Netanyahu) and various other people.”

“There are many other people that shouldn’t be looked at that way. But there is no indication that I am one of them at this moment,” Trump said.

Trump also said in July that the US campaign to dismantle the court was intended to defend Netanyahu and others from prosecution. He made the comments after Rubio told a cabinet meeting at Camp David that five countries had announced plans to quit the court since the United States launched a campaign earlier this month against what it says is a threat to US sovereignty.

articles.title: Trump calls Navi Pillay 'mystery person', laments Nobel snub
articles.summary:
Trump calls Navi Pillay 'mystery person', laments Nobel snub

US President Donald Trump has called this year’s Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay a “mystery person” and lamented the Nobel committee’s decision not to award him the prize, calling it “disgraceful and embarrassing”.

During a campaign rally in Syracuse, New York, Trump said: “I never heard of the person. Nobody did.”

Trump lashed out at Norway hours after the committee awarded this year’s prize to Pillay, a former International Criminal Court judge who led a UN enquiry that concluded Israel had committed genocide in Gaza.

Trump has expressed disappointment at not winning the prize every year of his presidency.

“This is an indelible stain on the country of Norway and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision,” he said.

He listed several conflicts he claimed a role in resolving and said he had helped prevent wars between North and South Korea, Japan and North Korea, and China and Taiwan, without providing evidence.

“The Nobel Peace Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilisation. And we will not forget, Norway,” he said.

archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the region remains critical due to ongoing fighting and strikes in Gaza, escalating tensions between the US and Iran, and incidents in the Persian Gulf including infrastructure attacks. Domestic and societal impacts on Israel and the wider Middle East continue to weigh heavily on economic stability and security prospects.
archive.forecast_cs: V nadcházejících dnech lze očekávat přetrvávající vojenské akce v Gaze a zvýšené diplomatické i vojenské napětí ve vztahu k Íránu a Perskému zálivu. Riziko náhlé eskalace zůstává vysoké.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, persistent military actions in Gaza and heightened diplomatic and military tensions regarding Iran and the Persian Gulf are expected. The risk of sudden escalation remains elevated.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu zůstává vysoce napjatá v důsledku pokračujících střetů v Gaze, izraelských vojenských operací v jižní Sýrii a incidentů na libanonské hranici. Pozornost poutá také vnitřní bezpečnostní riziko po odhaleném plánu na útok na letiště Ben Gurion a přetrvávající nestabilita v Iráku ohledně kontroly nad ozbrojenými milicemi.
archive.security_status_en: The regional security situation remains highly tense due to ongoing clashes in Gaza, Israeli military operations in southern Syria, and incidents along the Lebanese border. Attention is also drawn to domestic security risks following a thwarted attack plot targeting Ben Gurion Airport and persistent instability in Iraq regarding state control over armed militias.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující bezpečnostní operace v Sýrii a na libanonské hranici při zachování napjatého klidu v Gaze. Geopolitické riziko v Perském zálivu a ohledně Íránu zůstane zvýšené.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued security operations in Syria and along the Lebanese border are expected while a tense calm persists in Gaza. Geopolitical risk in the Persian Gulf and regarding Iran will remain elevated.
